ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The outside in the figure is square EFGH, and the left side is marked with side length 9 ft. A is on the bottom side HG, B is on the left side EH, C is on the top side EF, and D is on the right side FG. Connect A, B, C, and D to form the internally tilted quadrilateral ABCD. In the square, apart from ABCD, the four corners respectively form right triangles EBC, FCD, GDA, and HAB. Reasoning: The problem states that the vertices of ABCD divide each side of the square into two segments with a length ratio of 1:2. The side length of the square is 9 ft, so each side is divided into 3 ft and 6 ft. Each right triangle at a corner has two mutually perpendicular legs, with lengths 3 ft and 6 ft respectively, so the area of each triangle is (1/2)×3×6=9 square feet. The total area of the four corner triangles is 4×9=36 square feet. The area of square EFGH is 9×9=81 square feet, so the area of quadrilateral ABCD is 81−36=45 square feet. Therefore the area ratio of ABCD to EFGH is 45:81=5:9.

raw_record.question_text: In the figure, the vertices of quadrilateral ABCD intersect square EFGH and divide its sides into segments with measures that have a ratio of 1:2. Find the ratio between the areas of ABCD and EFGH.

method.method_draft: Use an area-complement argument. From the image, identify EFGH as the outer square, with A, B, C, D lying respectively on bottom, left, top, and right sides, forming four corner right triangles outside ABCD: EBC, FCD, GDA, and HAB. From the text, each side of the square is split in a 1:2 ratio; since the image labels the square side as 9 ft, the two segment lengths on each side are 3 ft and 6 ft. Each corner triangle has perpendicular legs 3 and 6, so each has area (1/2)(3)(6)=9 square feet. The four corner triangles total 36 square feet. The square area is 9^2=81 square feet, so area(ABCD)=81-36=45. Therefore area(ABCD):area(EFGH)=45:81=5:9.

method.method_draft: Use side-length/vector reasoning for the inner quadrilateral. From the image, take the square EFGH with side length 9 ft and note the cyclic placement of B, C, D, A on the left, top, right, and bottom sides. From the text, each side is divided in a 1:2 ratio, so let the shorter segment be x and the longer be 2x; since the square side is 9, x=3. Moving from B to C changes horizontally by 2x and vertically by x, so BC has length sqrt((2x)^2+x^2)=sqrt(5)x. Similarly, each side of ABCD has the same length, and adjacent side directions have slopes whose product is -1, so ABCD is a square. Thus area(ABCD)=(sqrt(5)x)^2=5x^2. The outer square area is (3x)^2=9x^2. Hence the ratio is 5x^2:9x^2=5:9.
